extracted.intended_audience: national IP offices, domestic courts, breeders, applicants, licensees, and industrial property practitioners in Member States
extracted.subtask_description: Legal standards and procedural rules for protection, licensing, forfeiture, enforcement, and registration of layout designs and plant variety certificates under the Annexes (conditions for protection, filing, opposition, ownership, licensing, remedies, and administrative procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for grant of non-voluntary license (layout designs)
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-voluntary license may be granted where (inter alia) working of the protected layout design on such territory does not meet the demand for the protected product on reasonable terms; or on account of the refusal of the holder of the layout design to grant reasonable commercial licenses on reasonable terms and procedures; or where establishment or development of industrial or commercial activities on such territory is unfairly and substantially prejudiced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding these grounds, a non-voluntary license may not be granted if the holder of the layout design provides legitimate reasons for the non-working (Article 27).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting court and domicile requirement for non-voluntary license
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for the grant of a non-voluntary license shall be made to the civil court of the domicile of the holder of the layout design or, if the holder is domiciled abroad, to the civil court of either his elected domicile or the place in which he has named an agent for the purposes of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only requests made by persons domiciled on the territory of a Member State shall be considered; the holder or his agent shall be informed without delay (Article 28(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of request for non-voluntary license
rubrics_metrics.description: The request shall contain: (a) the name and address of the requester; (b) the title of the layout design and the number of the layout design in respect of which a non-voluntary license is requested; (c) in the case of a non-voluntary license requested under Article 27, a statement by the requester in which he undertakes to work the layout design on the territory of one of the Member States in such a way as to meet the needs of the market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items are mandatory elements for admissibility of the request (Article 28(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting evidence for non-voluntary license request
rubrics_metrics.description: The request shall be accompanied by: (a) proof that the requester has previously approached the holder by registered letter requesting a contractual license but has been unable to obtain such a license subject to reasonable commercial terms and procedures and within a reasonable time; and (b) proof that the requester is capable of working the protected layout design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These attachments establish the requester’s bona fides and capacity to exploit the design (Article 28(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Court examination and correction opportunity for requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The civil court shall examine whether the request satisfies the requirements of Article 28; if it does not, the court shall reject it. Before rejecting the request, the court shall inform the requester of the deficiencies and shall allow him to make the necessary corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court provides an opportunity to cure defects before outright rejection (Article 29(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and participation in non-voluntary license proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request satisfies requirements, the civil court shall notify it to the holder and to any licensee whose name appears in the special register and invite them to submit observations in writing within three months; such observations shall be communicated to the requester. The court shall likewise notify any government authorities concerned and hold a hearing to which requester, holder, licensees and authorities shall be invited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-month written observation period and an oral hearing are required prior to decision (Article 29(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Court decision content when granting non-voluntary license
rubrics_metrics.description: If the non-voluntary license is granted, the decision shall specify (a) the scope of the license, specifying in particular the acts referred to in Article 7(b) of this Annex to which it extends and the period for which it is granted (a non-voluntary license under Article 27 cannot extend to importation); and (b) the amount of the remuneration to be paid by the licensee to the holder of the layout design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remuneration shall be equitable, due regard being had to all the circumstances of the case, and is subject to judicial revision at the request of either party (Article 29(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasoned written decision and publication of non-voluntary license
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision of the civil court shall be in writing and shall state the grounds on which it is based. The civil court shall convey the decision to the Organization, which shall register it and publish the decision and notify it to the requester, the holder and any registered licensee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court must record reasons; Organization handles registration and publication (Article 29(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights and obligations of non-voluntary licensee
rubrics_metrics.description: On expiry of the time limit for appeal or once an appeal decision upholds the grant, the licensee shall be authorized to exploit the protected layout design according to the terms of the decision and shall be required to pay the specified remuneration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant of non-voluntary license does not affect existing license contracts or other non-voluntary licenses; holder may not grant other licensees more favorable terms than those of the non-voluntary license (Article 30).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on sublicensing and transfer of non-voluntary license
rubrics_metrics.description: The beneficiary may not, without the consent of the holder, grant any third party permission to perform acts he is authorized to perform under the non-voluntary license. Notwithstanding this, a non-voluntary license may be transferred together with the business exploiting the design, but such transfer requires court authorization and a hearing of the holder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorized transfers must be notified to the Organization which will register and publish them; any authorized transfer binds the new licensee to the same obligations (Article 31).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment and withdrawal of non-voluntary license by court
rubrics_metrics.description: At request of the holder or beneficiary the court may amend the decision where new facts justify amendment. At request of the holder the court shall withdraw the non-voluntary license if (a) grounds for its grant have ceased to exist; (b) the beneficiary exceeds the scope of the license; or (c) the beneficiary is in arrears with payment of remuneration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cases (a) and (b) withdrawal may be requested by other licensees; if withdrawn under (a) beneficiary shall be allowed a reasonable period to cease working where immediate cessation would cause serious adverse consequences. Articles 28 and 29 procedures apply to amendment/withdrawal (Article 32).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals against non-voluntary license decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The holder, any registered licensee or any requester may, within one month from publication of the decision, appeal to the competent higher court against decisions under Articles 29(3), 30(1) or 31. An appeal contesting grant/authorization/amendment/withdrawal shall have staying effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision on appeal shall be notified to the Organization which shall register and publish it (Article 33).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of licensee to enforce against infringers when holder will not
rubrics_metrics.description: Any beneficiary of a contractual or non-voluntary license may request the holder to institute necessary legal proceedings; if within three months the holder refuses or fails to do so, the beneficiary of a registered license may institute such proceedings in his own name, without prejudice to the holder’s right to intervene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows licensee to protect rights if holder fails to act (Article 34(1)-(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of invalidation on non-voluntary license obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a final legal judgment declares the layout design invalid, the holder of the non-voluntary license shall be released from all obligations resulting from the decision granting him the non-voluntary license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidation relieves licensee of obligations tied to the invalid registration (Article 35).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex‑officio (ministerial) authorization to exploit layout design
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister responsible may decide, without the consent of the holder, that a public body or third party may exploit the layout design on the territory where (a) public interest (national security, food, health or other vital sectors) requires exploitation for public and non-commercial purposes; or (b) a judicial/administrative body holds that exploitation conditions are anti-competitive and Minister is convinced exploitation would end such practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorization limited in scope/duration to the purpose, principally intended for domestic market, non-exclusive, and gives rise to payment of appropriate remuneration taking into account economic value and need to combat anti‑competitive practices (Article 36(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required for ministerial authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: The request seeking authorization of the Minister shall be accompanied by proof that the holder has received from the requester an application for a contractual license but the requester has not been able to obtain a license under reasonable commercial conditions and within a reasonable period of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors the prior requirement for non-voluntary licenses to show attempted contractual negotiation (Article 36(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification, withdrawal and transfer of ministerial authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: At request of holder or beneficiary, the Minister may modify decision after hearing parties; Minister shall withdraw authorization at holder's request if convinced circumstances that led to decision no longer hold or beneficiary has not complied; but Minister may refuse withdrawal if legitimate interests of beneficiary justify maintaining it. Where a third party was designated, authorization may be transferred only with the enterprise exploiting the design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions of the Minister may be appealed to competent domestic court (Article 36(3)-(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture grounds for layout design registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Any concerned person may request forfeiture on grounds that: (a) the layout design is not eligible for protection under Articles 2 and 3; (b) the holder is not entitled to enjoy the protection provided for in Article 4; (d) if the layout design has been commercially exploited anywhere in the world prior to filing, such application was not filed within the time limit laid down in Articles 2(2) and 9(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If grounds affect only part of a layout design, forfeiture shall be effected only to the corresponding extent; request must be submitted to competent domestic court in writing and duly reasoned; forfeited registration deemed invalid as from date protection took effect; final decision notified to Organization for register and publication (Article 37).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim of ownership before domestic courts (layout designs)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the layout design has already been registered, claim of ownership shall be filed before the competent domestic court; the action shall lapse within three years from publication of the registration certificate. Action brought against a defendant who acts in bad faith is not subject to statutory limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final decision transferring registration shall be communicated to the Organization for recording and publication (Article 38).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of infringement for layout designs
rubrics_metrics.description: The carrying out of any act characterized unlawful under Article 5 shall constitute an infringement of the rights deriving from a layout design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines infringement by reference to acts made unlawful elsewhere in Annex (Article 39).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies available for infringement (layout designs)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the request of the holder, or of his licensee if certain conditions are met, the court may order any measure to stop the infringement or to prevent an imminent infringement, grant damages and order any other means of sanction provided by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits both interlocutory and final measures and damages depending on circumstances (Article 40).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of damages (layout designs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The court shall determine the amount of damages, taking into account the negative economic consequences, including loss of profits, suffered by the injured party, the profits made by the infringer and the moral prejudice caused to the rightholder as a result of the infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court weighs actual economic harm, infringer's profits and moral prejudice in quantifying damages (Article 41).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal penalties for knowing infringement (layout designs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who, knowingly and without authorization, carries out acts characterized as unlawful under Article 5 shall be guilty of an offense subject to imprisonment of one to three years and a fine of 1,000,000 to 6,000,000 CFA francs or to one of these two penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides for criminal sanctions in addition to civil remedies (Article 42).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional penalties including seizure and destruction
rubrics_metrics.description: The court may also order the seizure, confiscation and destruction of layout designs, integrated circuits or incriminated articles and of all equipment or tools having served specially to commit the offense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court may order physical remedies against infringing goods and tools (Article 43).

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent courts for layout design disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil actions relating to layout designs shall be brought before the competent domestic courts and judged as summary proceedings. If the accused in a criminal action raises questions concerning ownership, the competent court shall pass judgment thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies domestic courts and summary procedure rule (Article 44).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for plant variety protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Key definitions: 'plant variety certificate' (title to protect a new plant variety); 'plant variety' (plant grouping within a single botanical taxon of lowest rank defined by expression of characteristics from a given genotype, distinguishable by at least one characteristic, and considered a unit for propagation); 'essentially derived variety' (predominantly derived but retaining essential characteristics, clearly distinguishable; examples include mutants, selections, backcrossing, transformation); 'breeder' (person who bred, discovered and developed a variety, employer commissioning work, or successor in title).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitional criteria set the scope of who/what is protectable and who is entitled to rights (Annex X, Part I).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for protection of a plant variety
rubrics_metrics.description: A variety shall be: (a) new; (b) distinct; (c) uniform; (d) stable; and (e) given a denomination devised in accordance with the provisions of Article 23.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All five criteria are cumulative prerequisites for granting a plant variety certificate (Article 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty requirements for plant varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: A variety shall be deemed new if, on the filing date or priority date, reproductive or vegetative propagating material or harvested material has not been sold or otherwise disposed of to others, by or with consent of the breeder, for purposes of exploitation of the variety: (a) on the territories of Member States for more than one year; and (b) on territories of non-Member States for more than six years (trees and vines) or four years (other species).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty is lost if exploitation exceeds these time limits, subject to specified exceptions (Article 5(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions that do not cause loss of novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty shall not be lost by sale or disposal where it is due to an abuse to the detriment of the breeder; where it forms part of an agreement for transfer of rights; where it forms part of an agreement for multiplication on behalf of the breeder provided multiplied material reverts and is not used to produce another variety; where it forms part of field tests, laboratory trials or small-scale processing trials to evaluate the variety; where it fulfills statutory/regulatory obligations (e.g., entry in official catalogue); or where harvested material is a by-product sold anonymously for consumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies many common commercial and experimental exceptions preserving novelty (Article 5(2)(a)-(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctness criterion for plant varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: A variety shall be deemed distinct if it is clearly distinguishable from any other variety whose existence is a matter of common knowledge on the filing date or priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an application in any country or entry in a marketing catalogue that leads to a certificate/entry renders that variety a matter of common knowledge; evidence of common knowledge may include exploitation, entry in a register, or inclusion in a reference collection (Article 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity requirement for plant varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: A variety shall be deemed uniform if, subject to the variation expected on account of the particular features of its reproductive or vegetative propagation, it is sufficiently homogeneous in its relevant characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts expected biological variation while requiring sufficient homogeneity in relevant traits (Article 7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability requirement for plant varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: A variety shall be deemed stable if its relevant characteristics remain unchanged after repeated propagation or, where there is a particular cycle of reproduction or vegetative propagation, at the end of each such cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stability must be demonstrable over propagation cycles (Article 8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to a plant variety certificate (entitlement rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to a plant variety certificate shall belong to the breeder. It may be assigned or transferred by succession. The breeder shall be mentioned on certificate. In absence of proof to the contrary, the applicant shall be considered the person entitled. If several persons bred a variety jointly, right belongs to them jointly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes presumptions and transferability of entitlement (Article 9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint ownership provisions for plant variety certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint owners: each may exploit the certificate for own benefit subject to equitable compensation for others who do not exploit; each may take action for infringement for own exclusive benefit but must notify co-owners; each may grant non-exclusive licenses subject to equitable compensation and notification with offer of transfer of share; exclusive license requires agreement of all joint owners or court authorization; each joint owner may assign his share with right of first refusal for others for three months; provisions for relinquishment and division of relinquished share are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed mechanics for licenses, compensation, rights of first refusal, and dispute resolution by court are provided (Article 10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership for varieties produced on order
rubrics_metrics.description: Save where otherwise agreed by contract, the right to a plant variety certificate for a variety bred in fulfillment of an order under a business contract shall belong to the person who ordered the variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default rule subject to contractual override (Article 11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Varieties bred by employees (employer/employee rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an employee breeds a variety: (a) if breeding is part of employment duties including inventive activity, the variety belongs to the employer and employee entitled to additional remuneration; (b) if employee not required to engage in inventive activity but used employer's techniques/facilities/information, employer may claim ownership or exploit rights subject to fair payment to employee; (c) all other varieties belong to the employee. Employee must inform employer; agreements must be in writing; employer waiver transfers right to employee; rules apply to State employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides multi-factor test for employer entitlement and mandates written agreements and information-sharing (Article 12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requirements for plant variety certificate applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Application shall be filed with the Organization or national service and the file shall contain: (a) an application bearing name and prescribed info relating to applicant, breeder and agent; identification of botanical taxon (Latin and common name); denomination proposed or provisional designation; (b) a succinct technical description of the variety; (c) proof of payment of required fees; (d) an unstamped private power of attorney if represented by an agent; and (e) document of priority, if any. Documents shall be in one of the working languages of the Organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may withdraw until application is ruled to satisfy conditions necessary for certificate issuance (Article 13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claiming procedure and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: To claim priority under the International Convention, applicant must submit application to the Organization within 12 months of earlier filing. Applicant must attach or submit within six months a written statement specifying date/number/country of earlier filing and a certified copy of the earlier application. Where multiple earlier applications exist, priority may be based only on the earliest. Priority deems application as filed on date of first application for protection conditions; applicant may request deferment of examination for not more than two years from expiry of priority term or three years from filing date of first application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit required items in time results in loss of priority; items received more than six months after filing are inadmissible (Article 14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadmissibility for non-payment of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: No application shall be admissible if it is not accompanied by a document proving payment of the prescribed fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment proof is a formal prerequisite to admissibility (Article 15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility conditions and filing date allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall allocate as the filing date the date of receipt provided that at time of receipt the application contains: (i) information to establish identity of applicant; (ii) the description of the variety; and (iii) proof of payment of filing and publication fees. If required items are missing, Organization shall request corrections and allocate as filing date the date of receipt of corrections; failure to correct within time allowed results in application deemed not filed. Other defects are invited to be rectified; non-rectification results in deemed not filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiates essential items that fix filing date from other rectifiable defects (Article 16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of plant variety applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall publish a notice of filing of the application containing the items mentioned in Article 13(2)(a) and (b) (applicant info, taxon identification, denomination and succinct technical description).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication triggers periods for objections and claims of ownership (Article 17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection procedure to issuance of plant variety certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Once published, any person may file written and reasoned objections within three months (fee charged). Objections may be filed exclusively to assert that the variety is not new, distinct, uniform or stable or that the applicant is not entitled to protection. Organization sends copy to applicant who may respond within three months, renewable once. Organization may hear parties before ruling; ruling subject to appeal to High Commission of Appeal within 60 days from notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines limited scope of valid objections and procedural timelines (Article 18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim of ownership proceedings before the Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: When a person not entitled files an application, the person entitled may claim ownership before the Organization within three months from publication. The Organization shall send a copy of the statement of claim to the applicant/agent who may reply within a once-renewable three-month period; the reply shall be forwarded to the claimant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organization will, on request, take further procedural steps before deciding (Article 19, partial).
